subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics, Year 9
syllabus: Victorian Curriculum F-10 Version 2.0: Mathematics, Level 9

points.title: The real number system
points.brief: Natural numbers sit inside the integers, which sit inside the rationals, and the rationals and irrationals together make the real numbers.

points.title: Negative indices
points.brief: A negative index means the reciprocal, so 2⁻³ = 1/2³ = 1/8.

points.title: Index laws with variables
points.brief: The index laws work with letters too, so 3x² × 4x³ = 12x⁵ and (2a³)² = 4a⁶.

points.title: Scientific notation for large numbers
points.brief: A large number is written as a number from 1 to less than 10 times a power of 10, such as 384,000 = 3.84 × 10⁵.

points.title: Scientific notation for small numbers
points.brief: A small number uses a negative power of 10, such as 0.00052 = 5.2 × 10⁻⁴.

points.title: Expanding binomial products
points.brief: Multiply each term in the first bracket by each term in the second, such as (x + 3)(x + 5) = x² + 8x + 15.

points.title: Perfect squares and the difference of two squares
points.brief: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², and (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b², where the middle terms cancel.

points.title: Factorising monic quadratics
points.brief: For x² + bx + c, find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b, such as x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4).

points.title: Factorising a difference of two squares
points.brief: Spot two perfect squares with a minus between them and write the pair of brackets, such as x² - 25 = (x + 5)(x - 5).

points.title: Gradient of a line
points.brief: Gradient is rise over run. It is positive going up to the right, negative going down, zero for a flat line and undefined for a vertical one.

points.title: Gradient-intercept form
points.brief: In y = mx + c, m is the gradient and c is where the line crosses the y-axis.

points.title: Sketching a line from its intercepts
points.brief: Set x = 0 to find the y-intercept and y = 0 to find the x-intercept, then draw the line through the two points.

points.title: Midpoint of an interval
points.brief: The midpoint's coordinates are the averages of the two x values and of the two y values.

points.title: Distance between two points
points.brief: Use Pythagoras on the horizontal and vertical gaps between the points, d = √((x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²).

points.title: Graphs of quadratic functions
points.brief: A quadratic makes a parabola with a turning point and an axis of symmetry. A positive x² term opens upwards, a negative one downwards.

points.title: Changing a and c in y = ax² + c
points.brief: A larger a makes the parabola narrower, a negative a flips it, and c moves it up or down.

points.title: The null factor law
points.brief: If two factors multiply to zero, one of them must be zero, so (x - 2)(x + 5) = 0 gives x = 2 or x = -5.

points.title: Solving quadratics from a graph
points.brief: The solutions of ax² + bx + c = 0 are the x-intercepts of the parabola, which may be two, one or none.

points.title: Simple interest
points.brief: Interest on the starting amount only, I = Prn, so it grows by the same amount each year.

points.title: Surface area of a prism
points.brief: Add the areas of all the faces, which a net shows laid flat.

points.title: Volume of a cylinder
points.brief: A cylinder is a prism with a circle as its cross-section, so V = πr²h.

points.title: Surface area of a cylinder
points.brief: Two circles and a curved rectangle whose length is the circumference, so SA = 2πr² + 2πrh.

points.title: Volume of composite solids
points.brief: Split a solid into prisms and cylinders, find each volume, and add them, or subtract a hole.

points.title: Naming the sides of a right-angled triangle
points.brief: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle. The opposite and adjacent sides are named from the angle being used.

points.title: Sine, cosine and tangent ratios
points.brief: sin is opposite over hypotenuse, cos is adjacent over hypotenuse and tan is opposite over adjacent, the same for every triangle with that angle.

points.title: Finding a side with trigonometry
points.brief: Choose the ratio linking the known side and the unknown side to the angle, then rearrange to find the unknown.

points.title: Finding an angle with trigonometry
points.brief: Work out the ratio of two sides, then use the inverse function on a calculator, such as tan⁻¹, to find the angle.

points.title: Enlargements
points.brief: An enlargement multiplies every length by the scale factor but keeps the angles and the shape the same.

points.title: Using similar triangles
points.brief: Matching sides of similar triangles are in the same ratio, so a known pair gives the scale factor to find an unknown side.

points.title: Scale drawings and maps
points.brief: A scale such as 1:50,000 means 1 cm on the map is 50,000 cm, or 500 m, on the ground.

points.title: Direct proportion
points.brief: Two quantities are in direct proportion when one is always a fixed multiple of the other, y = kx, so the graph is a straight line through the origin.

points.title: Absolute error of a measurement
points.brief: A measurement is only as exact as its smallest unit, so the absolute error is half that unit, such as ±0.5 cm for a length to the nearest cm.

points.title: Histograms
points.brief: A histogram groups numerical data into equal class intervals, with bars that touch to show the frequency in each.

points.title: Back-to-back stem-and-leaf plots
points.brief: Two data sets share one stem, with leaves going left and right, so their centres and spreads can be compared.

points.title: Skewed, symmetric and bimodal shapes
points.brief: Symmetric data is balanced, skewed data has a long tail to one side, and bimodal data has two peaks.

points.title: Comparing two distributions
points.brief: Compare data sets by their centre (mean or median), their spread (range) and their shape, and say what the differences mean.

points.title: Choosing a display for data
points.brief: Column graphs suit categories, histograms and stem-and-leaf plots suit numerical data, and line graphs suit change over time.

points.title: Misleading surveys and graphs
points.brief: How a biased sample, a leading question or an axis that does not start at zero can make results look stronger than they are.

points.title: Outcomes of two-step experiments
points.brief: List every outcome of two steps, such as rolling two dice, in a table or tree diagram, and count to find probabilities.

points.title: With and without replacement
points.brief: Without replacement, the first pick changes what is left, so the probabilities on the second branch change.

points.title: And, inclusive or, exclusive or
points.brief: With "and", both events happen. With inclusive "or", either or both happen. With exclusive "or", one happens but not both.

points.title: Estimating probability by simulation
points.brief: When a probability cannot be worked out exactly, repeat a model of the situation many times and use the relative frequency.
